Figure 1:Comparison of training paradigms and learning signals. Outcome-based group RL assigns trajectory-level credit, state-level group RL compares sampled actions at shared states, and OPD distills a single corrective action.
In contrast, SERO restores a state reached by the current policy, executes a multi-step oracle continuation, and applies policy-reachability weighting to downstream action losses.

Figure 2:Overview of SERO.
(a) The behavior policy collects on-policy rollouts for the base RL objective.
(b) From a selected policy-visited state, SERO restores the environment, executes an oracle continuation under the same remaining horizon, and computes a detached improvement gate.
(c) The frozen behavior policy provides compatibility scores used to form policy-reachability weights for downstream oracle-action losses.
(d) The root-averaged auxiliary loss is combined with the base RL loss in one policy update. The oracle and environment restoration are used only during training, and only the learned policy is used at inference.
